text: Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square, and three cubits high.
Make horns for it on its four corners; the horns shall be of one piece with it, and overlay it with bronze.
Make its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans. Make all its utensils of bronze.
Make a grating for it of bronze network, and on the network make four bronze rings at its four corners.
Set it under the ledge of the altar, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
The poles are to be inserted into the rings, so that they are along the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make the altar hollow, of boards. They shall make it just as you were shown on the mountain.

versions.text: Make the altar hollow, of boards. It shall be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew ends with an active plural verb, 'so they shall make it,' which the passive rendering flattens; the active form also reads well aloud.

text: Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard shall have curtains of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long on that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands shall be of silver.
Likewise along the north side there shall be curtains a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands shall be of silver.
For the width of the courtyard on the west side there shall be curtains fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.

versions.text: Across the width of the courtyard on the west side there shall be curtains fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
versions.explanation: 'Across the width' adds a preposition not in the Hebrew and reads awkwardly; 'For the width' matches the parallel construction of verse 13.

text: The width of the courtyard on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
On one side of the entrance there shall be curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
For the gate of the courtyard there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases.

versions.text: For the gate of the courtyard there shall be a curtain twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of a weaver, with four posts and four bases.
versions.explanation: רֹקֵם denotes an embroiderer, distinct from חֹשֵׁב (designer/weaver) and אֹרֵג (weaver). Using 'weaver' blurs the distinction made elsewhere in the tabernacle instructions.

versions.text: For the gate of the courtyard there shall be a curtain twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases.
versions.explanation: מָסָךְ is a hanging screen at an entrance, distinct from the קְלָעִים (courtyard curtains) and from the inner פָּרֹכֶת. Rendering it 'screen' preserves the distinction the chapter makes between the three, which is also the concern noted in the revision of v. 21. 'Curtain' is a possible rendering but blurs the terminology.

text: All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide throughout, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and bronze bases.
All the equipment used in the service of the tabernacle, and all its pegs and all the pegs of the courtyard, shall be of bronze.
You shall command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that the lamp may be kept burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it before the LORD from evening until morning. This shall be a lasting statute for their generations, binding on the Israelites.

versions.text: In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that stands before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it before the LORD from evening until morning. This shall be a lasting statute for the Israelites throughout their generations.
versions.explanation: Distinguish the inner veil (פָּרֹכֶת) from the courtyard curtains (קְלָעִים/מָסָךְ) already called 'curtain' in this chapter; also מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל indicates the statute is binding on/among the Israelites.

versions.text: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the ark of the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it before the LORD from evening until morning. This shall be a lasting statute among the Israelites throughout their generations.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says only הָעֵדֻת, 'the testimony'; 'ark of' is an added word not in the text (the ark is אֲרוֹן הָעֵדֻת elsewhere, but not here). Also, keeping לְדֹרֹתָם before מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל follows the Hebrew order and makes clear that the obligation rests on the Israelites.
